title: GDP grew 7.8% in April-June, led by services and investment
dek: Investment grew 11.9%, about double the pace of a year earlier, while farm growth slowed.
author: sarah-qureshi

body.text: India's real GDP grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, up from 6.9% in the same quarter a year earlier, according to MoSPI estimates released on 31 August. Nominal GDP, which includes inflation, grew 10.3%. Real gross value added (GVA) grew 8.2%.
Services and construction did the lifting

The services sector grew 10.0%, against 8.0% a year earlier. Within it, financial, real estate and professional services grew 12.1%, and public administration, defence and other services 7.5%. Trade, hotels, transport and communication slowed to 8.5% from 9.8%.
In industry, manufacturing grew 9.2% and construction 7.7%. Electricity, gas and water supply grew 8.9% after shrinking 1.8% a year earlier. Mining contracted 2.4%.
Farming was the weak spot. Agriculture, livestock, forestry and fishing grew 3.6%, slower than 4.4% a year ago.

On the spending side, gross fixed capital formation, which measures investment in buildings, machinery and infrastructure, grew 11.9% against 5.8% a year earlier. Private consumption grew 7.1%, up from 6.8%.
These estimates use the new 2022-23 base year. Estimates for July-September are due on 30 November 2026.
